Definition: full (literally or figuratively) or filling (literally); also (concretely) fulness; adverbially, fully
BiblicalUsage: Male is full, filled, fulness, and it is full of everything from houses to hearts. Deuteronomy 6:11 promises houses full of all good things which Israel did not fill, and Deuteronomy 33:23 says Naphtali is full with the blessing of the LORD, while Deuteronomy 34:9 says Joshua the son of Nun was full of the spirit of wisdom. Ruth 1:21 turns the word over: Naomi says, I went out full, and the LORD hath brought me home again empty.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that this word measures a life: full of blessing in Deuteronomy 33:23, full of wisdom in Deuteronomy 34:9, and empty in Ruth 1:21 until God fills it again. My position is that Naomi's emptiness is the honest half of the word, because she names it plainly, and God fills it by the end of the book.
